subject.title: [Feature]:Support per-agent command lanes for multi-agent deployments

question: What public scheduler/config contract should OpenClaw use for foreground per-agent command lane isolation on shared gateways?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates new public config and scheduler semantics that must settle lane ownership, aggregate caps, and the request trust boundary before implementation.

options.title: Approve trusted per-agent lanes
options.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned foreground lanes while keeping a separate aggregate safety cap.

options.title: Fold into a unified scheduler
options.body: Defer this issue until foreground, subagent, hook, browser/workload, and queue-observability requests can share one coordinated scheduler model.

options.title: Decline new core lane config
options.body: Keep the shared main lane and document separate gateway processes as the supported isolation pattern for heavy agents.

recommendation.title: Approve trusted per-agent lanes
recommendation.body: Add a validated agent/defaults config surface that maps agents or groups to server-owned foreground lanes while keeping a separate aggregate safety cap.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history and prior review signal for command-lane concurrency and config direction points to this person.
